rationale:
Evidence: all three raced designs (iterations 0, 1 and 3) left the track in all 60 trials. On the s-bend, progress was 0.040 and max_error about 0.061 to 0.062 in every race, whatever kp, kd, base_speed or sensor spacing was used. A failure point that does not move with gains or speed points to a fixed early event, most likely a sensing limit at the track edge, so I keep the wide-array geometry as the one change aimed at that limit.

Accepted from the round-2 critique: (1) The ki change from 0.1 to 0 was unexplained. I set ki to 0.02, the value of the last raced design, so the only controller changes against that race are base_speed, kp and kd. Its maximum contribution is about 14 PWM, so it is a bias trim only. (2) Gain matching is kept: 7 sensors at 0.025 m spacing give about 13.3 signal units per metre, and kp 5.5 keeps steering authority near 73 units per metre, close to the 75 of iteration 1. (3) The visibility limit is accepted: outer sensors see tape only beyond about 0.054 m offset, so they add little before the robot is near the 0.06 m limit. I state this as a limit of the layout.

Partly accepted: kd. The critique's noise estimate for kd 0.4 (about 280 PWM) is a guess built on an assumed signal jitter, not measured data. Even so, the noise risk is real, so I lower kd from 0.4 to 0.3 to bound the derivative term while keeping meaningful damping. Rejected: lowering base_speed further as the main test, because completion needs about 1.5 m/s and a 0.9 run cannot finish. base_speed stays at 1.0, the speed already raced, so the sensing change is the one new variable against it.

Summary of changes against the last raced design (iteration 3): sensor layout widened to 7 sensors at 0.025 m spacing from x -0.075 to 0.075 with y 0.06 and footprint 0.016; mass 0.6; kp 5.5; kd 0.3; ki 0.02; base_speed 1.0. Line loss stays last_direction.

Expected result (guess): max_error below 0.06 and progress above 0.04 on the s-bend. Decision rule: if max_error is below 0.05 with zero line-loss events on the s-bend, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 toward 1.5. If progress is still 0.040 on the s-bend, the cause is a start or entry transient, and the next test should change the line-loss rule (search_left or search_right) or the start, not the gains.
